reasons: Correctly identifies Section 4(c) as the only inbound licence to us and accurately characterises the gaps against the preferred position: no Affiliates/contractors named, perpetual but not stated irrevocable, and silent on transfer while Section 10 bars assignment without consent.

Redline reaches the playbook position with targeted insertions — licensee extended to Company, its Affiliates (with a workable control-based definition, since 'Affiliates' is undefined) and contractors acting on our behalf; 'irrevocable' added alongside 'perpetual'; and an express carve-out from Section 10 permitting transfer to a successor by merger/acquisition/asset sale.

Edited clause remains grammatical and preserves the existing royalty-free, non-exclusive, sublicensable rights and use-purpose scope (broadened only to include Affiliates' business operations); the 0.585 changed-character ratio is explained by the three distinct rule-required changes rather than unnecessary rewriting.

Deterministic checks all pass (affiliate coverage, no at-will revocation, operation applies), and the deviation (not walk-away) classification is correct because the grant is not expressly revocable at Contractor's discretion.
Comment is concise, first-person plural, cites the playbook position, explains the business rationale, and offers the written-notice fallback for Affiliate coverage without lecturing.
